title: Upgrade/rollback-safe migrations for Private observability dashboards + metrics
creator: Talia Benson
body:
## Context
Private installs ship a versioned "minimum observability pack" (Prometheus rules + Grafana dashboards + log pipeline defaults) via Helm/installer. We have active work to standardize metric names/labels (ENG-19143 / PR-18503) and to ship dashboards (observability-pack PR-18341) + alerts (PR-18356/18372).

We must ensure upgrades and rollbacks do not break:
- dashboards (panels go blank / errors due to renamed series)
- alert rules (query errors due to missing metrics)
- recording rules (downstream dashboards/alerts rely on them)

This ticket defines and implements an upgrade/rollback-safe migration strategy for:
1) metric/label renames (including deprecations)
2) dashboard schema changes (datasource UID changes, variable names, query edits)
3) rule file refactors (recording rules renamed, group changes)

The goal is to be able to upgrade across at least N-1 versions and rollback to N-1 without losing observability. This is particularly critical for air-gapped/on-prem customers that upgrade less frequently and rely on stable dashboards during incident response.

## Requirements / non-negotiables
- Upgrades must not introduce Prometheus rule evaluation errors ("unknown metric" / parse errors) by default.
- Dashboards must continue to render at least core panels (golden signals) across upgrade + rollback.
- Any breaking metric changes must have an explicit, documented migration path.
- Avoid high-cardinality workarounds (no per-tenant/per-route back-compat labels that would blow up TSDB).

## Proposal (implementation plan)
### A) Metrics: compatibility window via recording rule aliases
When a metric is renamed or label set changes, we will maintain a compatibility window by producing *alias recording rules* in Prometheus for one full release (N and N+1), then remove in N+2.

Pattern:
- New canonical metric name: `redwood:runtime:request_latency_seconds:p95`
- Back-compat alias for old name expected by existing dashboards/alerts:
  - `record: redwood_runtime_request_latency_seconds_p95`
  - `expr: redwood:runtime:request_latency_seconds:p95`

Guidelines:
- Prefer aliasing via recording rules over emitting duplicate application metrics.
- If label sets changed (e.g., `model` label removed/capped), alias rules must aggregate/downgrade old shape safely:
  - old expected series: `...{model="..."}`
  - new canonical: aggregated without model
  - alias should use `sum without(model)(...)` or `max without(model)(...)` depending on metric type.
- Any alias rules must be in a dedicated group `redwood_private_compat` with a prominent comment header and removal version.

### B) Labels: stable label keys with bounded cardinality
We are standardizing labels in ENG-19143. For migrations, we commit to:
- stable label keys across minor releases (`cluster`, `namespace`, `service`, `pod`) 
- optional/capped labels for Private (`route_group`, `model_family`) rather than raw `route`/`model`

If a dashboard currently uses a soon-to-be-removed label, we update the dashboard to prefer canonical metrics first, but keep an `or` fallback for one release:
- `new_query OR old_query`
Example:
- `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redwood:runtime:request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))
  or
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redwood_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))`

### C) Dashboards: versioning + deterministic provisioning
Dashboards are provisioned by the pack (not edited in-place as "mutable" dashboards). For upgrades/rollbacks:
- Dashboards will be deployed with stable `uid` values per dashboard.
- Folder name must remain stable: `Redwood Private (Minimum)`.
- Datasource references must use datasource *name* (e.g., `Prometheus`) rather than hard-coded UID, since UID can differ across customer Grafana installs.
- Dashboard schema changes are allowed, but must preserve core panel IDs and variable names where possible to reduce Grafana "panel not found" issues for deep links.

Implementation:
- Add a `dashboards/manifest.json`-like text manifest in the pack repo (even if not consumed by code) that records:
  - dashboard UID
  - dashboard slug
  - introduced version
  - last breaking change version (if any)
  - deprecated queries (old metrics) + planned removal

### D) Rule files: avoid group/name churn; add CI checks
Rule evaluation failures were a top source of noisy upgrades in prior private installs. We will:
- Keep recording rule names stable once introduced.
- If a recording rule must change, create a new canonical recording rule and preserve old name as an alias (same approach as metrics).
- Add CI checks in the smoke-test harness (ENG-19156 / PR-18544) to assert:
  1) `promtool check rules` passes
  2) Prometheus shows zero rule evaluation errors after install
  3) Dashboards render at least the runtime overview + control plane overview without "no data" for basic smoke workload

### E) Upgrade/rollback test matrix
Minimum matrix for this ticket:
- Upgrade: N-1 -> N (charts + pack)
- Rollback: N -> N-1
Environments:
- VPC-like (online)
- on-prem-like (air-gapped bundle artifacts present)

We will treat this as a gate for GA readiness (ENG-19159).

## Work items
1) Document the compatibility contract (N-1 supported, alias removal in N+2) in the internal runbook and release notes.
2) Implement `redwood_private_compat` rule group:
   - alias rules for renamed runtime metrics
   - alias rules for any renamed alerts/recordings used by dashboards
3) Update dashboards to prefer canonical metrics and include one-release fallback (`or`) where necessary.
4) Add unit-ish checks to CI (promtool + dashboard lint):
   - verify stable dashboard UIDs
   - reject datasource UID hard-coding
   - ensure dashboards reference canonical recording rules first
5) Execute upgrade/rollback tests using the smoke test harness and capture results.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Upgrading Private install from N-1 to N results in:
  - zero Prometheus rule parse/eval errors
  - runtime + control plane dashboards populate for a basic inference workload
- [ ] Rolling back from N to N-1 results in:
  - dashboards still render and do not hard-fail due to missing metrics
  - alerts remain evaluatable (even if thresholds differ)
- [ ] Compatibility rules are clearly marked and have removal version noted
- [ ] Release notes include a "Metrics & dashboard compatibility" section with any known changes

## References
- Metric standardization PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-18503-standardize-metric-labels-and-reduce-cardinality-for-private.json
- Dashboard bundle PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-18341-add-private-minimum-pack-dashboard-bundle.json
- Alert rules PRs: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-18356-add-private-prometheus-alert-rules-latency-and-availability.json, pr-18372-add-gpu-saturation-and-oom-alerts.json
- Helm wiring PR: sources/github/redwood-helm-charts/pr-18405-wire-observability-pack-into-private-values.json
- Installer validation PR: sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr-18422-add-observability-preflight-and-postinstall-validation.json

## Open questions
- Do we guarantee N-1 compatibility at the *pack* level, or tied to *installer* versions? Current assumption: tied to installer release train; pack version pinned by chart.
- For customers who edit dashboards manually in Grafana: we do not support preserving custom dashboards, but stable metric aliases should still help.
comments: 2025-07-10 (Talia Benson): Creating this as a blocker for GA readiness. We have at least one prior support case where dashboards went blank after upgrade due to metric rename + Grafana datasource UID mismatch. Need a formal compatibility strategy here.

2025-07-15 (Allison Grant): +1 on alias recording rules vs emitting duplicate app metrics. Please keep compat rules in separate group and timebox removal; otherwise they become permanent baggage. Also ensure any aggregation is semantically correct (counters vs gauges).

2025-07-18 (Thomas Baird): Watch out for using `or` in dashboard queries everywhere; it can double query load in Prometheus. Suggest using it only on a small set of panels (golden signals) and only for one release window.

2025-07-24 (Dylan Brooks): Drafted a dashboard lint rule to block datasource UID references. Will add to smoke harness. Also planning to freeze dashboard UIDs going forward (existing ones need to be checked in the bundle).

2025-08-01 (Rafael Mendes): From SRE side: treat "rule evaluation errors" as a hard fail in CI for the pack. We've seen upgrades where Prometheus is healthy but rules are broken; oncall experience is terrible.

2025-08-08 (Nadia Rahman): Instrumentation changes in PR-18503 remove `model` label in Private mode. For migration: dashboards should pivot to `model_family` where available, but otherwise aggregate. Please document explicitly in release notes so customers don't think we're losing fidelity accidentally.

2025-08-14 (Sahana Iyer): CI in INT-11804 is flaky due to Prometheus startup timing; but we can still validate rules and a subset of dashboard panels. Suggest: wait-for-ready + query `/api/v1/rules` for errors before asserting dashboard data.

2025-08-21 (Dylan Brooks): Implementation mostly done; requesting review on compat rule group + dashboard fallback changes. Remaining: run full rollback test on air-gapped path once Connor provides latest bundle manifest.
